Fit several models and compare them

Source: R/compare.R
compare_models.Rd

Fits each model with estimate_parameters and returns a table ranked by AIC.

Usage

compare_models(
  data,
  models = c("gaussian", "t", "leverage", "skew_gaussian", "skew_gaussian_leverage",
    "skew_t", "skew_t_leverage"),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A vector of observations.

models

Character vector of models. See estimate_parameters. The default is all models.

...

Additional arguments passed to estimate_parameters. silent = TRUE is used unless you set it.

Value

A data.table with one row for each model, ordered by AIC, and the columns model, n_par, log_lik, aic, bic, delta_aic (the difference to the smallest AIC), converged, pd_hessian and message. The fitted models are in the attribute "fits", a named list of stochvolTMB objects.

Details

The table also shows if the optimizer converged and if the Hessian is positive definite. A model that fails one of these checks has unreliable estimates and standard errors, even when its AIC is small. A model that gives an error is reported with NA values and the error message.

Examples

# \donttest{
comparison <- compare_models(spy$log_return, models = c("gaussian", "t", "leverage"))
comparison
#>       model n_par  log_lik       aic       bic delta_aic converged pd_hessian
#>      <char> <int>    <num>     <num>     <num>     <num>    <lgcl>     <lgcl>
#> 1: leverage     4 11808.43 -23608.85 -23584.18    0.0000      TRUE       TRUE
#> 2:        t     4 11729.85 -23451.69 -23427.02  157.1599      TRUE       TRUE
#> 3: gaussian     3 11718.29 -23430.57 -23412.07  178.2778      TRUE       TRUE
#>                     message
#>                      <char>
#> 1: relative convergence (4)
#> 2: relative convergence (4)
#> 3: relative convergence (4)
best <- attr(comparison, "fits")[[comparison$model[1]]]
# }
